title: Tooltips
subtopics: Accessible usage and limitations on mobile devices
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of tooltips and when it is appropriate.
Apply tooltip triggers using the documented Bootstrap 5.3 pattern.
Check placement options and identify one likely failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study tooltips and connect it to a small implementation or review task. The included subtopics preserve the attached Bootstrap curriculum outline.
content.why_it_matters: Tooltips affects interface feedback and sometimes focus or motion. Keep the trigger and target relationship explicit, provide an accessible name, and ensure the user can understand and dismiss the state.

content_blocks.code:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Bootstrap lesson example</title>
  <link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
</head>
<body>
  <main class="container py-4">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="A concise helpful hint">Focus or hover for a tooltip</button>
  </main>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
  <script>document.querySelectorAll('[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"]').forEach((element) => new bootstrap.Tooltip(element));</script>
</body>
</html>

content_blocks.title: Version and implementation note
content_blocks.text: Tooltips and popovers require JavaScript initialization and Popper positioning. The Bootstrap bundle includes Popper; initialize dynamically inserted elements deliberately.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating tooltips as a visual-only change.
common_mistakes.why: A class or style does not automatically add semantic meaning, application logic, or secure server behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the appropriate HTML semantics and verify the actual interaction.

common_mistakes.problem: Checking only the default viewport or happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Responsive changes and interaction states can reveal issues that are not visible in a single screenshot.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat the task at a narrow and a wide viewport and include keyboard/error state checks where relevant.
